sovereign_country.strategic_role: 制造业产业链转移第一站、保税加工（EPE）设立首选

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam and the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments
Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Singapore and the Government of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam on Promotion and Protection of Investments
Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam on the Promotion and Protection of Investment
Agreement between the Government of Japan and the Government of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam on the Liberalization, Promotion and Protection of Investment

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15 (effective 1 March 2023); Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP dated 10 May 2023 detailing implementation of the Anti-Money Laundering Law; Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; relevant State Bank of Viet Nam implementing circulars and guidance on AML/CFT compliance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder (e.g., Companies Registry Hong Kong, ACRA Singapore, UK Companies House)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille obtained from the competent authority in the issuing jurisdiction; for non-Hague Convention states, consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of Viet Nam

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the bio-data page of the passport of each natural person identified as the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (direct or indirect holding of 25% or more)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport or Immigration Authority of the UBO's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of issue followed by Hague Apostille, or consular legalization by a Vietnamese diplomatic mission if the issuing state is not an Apostille Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited financial statements or income and capital evidence of the foreign investor for the last two fiscal years (to substantiate commercial substance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Independent registered external auditor in the investor's jurisdiction or competent tax/revenue authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the issuing state is not a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention, consular legalization by Viet Nam's competent consular office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized Power of Attorney appointing a licensed Vietnamese law firm or incorporation agent as representative in the enterprise registration process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or equivalent public attestation authority in the place of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate General of Viet Nam overseas, or Hague Apostille where both the executing state and Viet Nam are Contracting States to the Apostille Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and UBOs against the State Bank of Viet Nam AML reporting list, the Financial Action Task Force public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, U.S. OFAC SDN List and non-SDN sanctions lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Viet Nam domestic regulatory debarment lists, and Vietnamese criminal and police records. PEP status must be verified at a granular level through independent background sources, with source of wealth and source of funds documentation required for all PEPs and individuals connected to state-owned enterprises.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) – dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name must be in the Vietnamese language and written in the Latin alphabet with all Vietnamese diacritical marks. It must consist of the legal form designation (e.g., 'Công ty TNHH' for a limited liability company) followed by a proper name. Foreign-language names are permissible only as an exact translation or transliteration of the Vietnamese proper name, presented in a smaller typeface beneath the Vietnamese name. The name may contain only Vietnamese alphabet letters, numerals, and allowed symbols; it must not include words, symbols, or characters that are ambiguous, unlawful, contrary to national traditions, or that misleadingly imply governmental or ministerial affiliation. An abbreviated name may be derived in accordance with Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words and expressions associated with state administrative organs (e.g., 'Bộ', 'Cơ quan', 'Tổng cục', 'Sở', 'Phường') when not licensed as part of a permitted specialized name
Military and public-security designations (e.g., 'Quân đội', 'Công an', 'Lực lượng vũ trang') without written approval of the Ministry of Defence or Ministry of Public Security
Terms reserved for licensed financial activities (e.g., 'Ngân hàng', 'Chứng khoán', 'Bảo hiểm', 'Quỹ đầu tư') absent the specific statutory business license
Vulgar, discriminatory, or honorific-superlative expressions, or names that infringe prior trademark or business name rights
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise in the same provincial registration area or nationally protected enterprise name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 05 working days of receipt of the application, the business registration agency under the Department of Planning and Investment must issue either an Enterprise Registration Certificate or a written refusal stating the legal ground. Upon name rejection, the applicant may (i) amend and resubmit a revised name application via the National Business Registration Portal, or (ii) file a reconsideration request with the same business registration agency within 10 working days of the refusal. If the registration agency still rejects the name, the applicant may file an administrative complaint to the provincial People's Committee under Law No. 02/2011/QH13 on Complaints, and further seek judicial review at the provincial People's Court. The appeal is subject to no statutory dossier fee; legal representation fees apply at agreed market rates.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permissible as the sole statutory registered address of a foreign-invested limited liability company. The registered address must be a physical, rentable premises in Viet Nam where the statutory legal representative, corporate records, and accounting documents can be inspected. A shared-workspace or serviced-office address may be accepted so long as it constitutes a physical location under the service provider's lease and the provider consents to serve as the point of legal and administrative delivery. For a data-center colocation lessor, the statutory head office may be separate from the rack-space colocation facilities, but it must nevertheless be a fixed physical office address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 30% within the first two years of operation for a physically occupied dedicated head office; risk increases to above 60% if a virtual or co-working address is used, and to 75% where the registered office is the sole connection with the business. Colocation operators face additional inspection rights by the Department of Information and Communications and data-competency authorities under cyber-security review, notwithstanding the absence of a separate statutory license.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation due diligence report: corporate structure verification, UBO piercing, PEP and OFAC/UN sanctions screening, company name search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged licensed law firm / corporate intelligence provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: fixed professional fee at US$ 300–450 per hour based on entity structure and beneficial-ownership complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise registration name clearance and application filing via the National Business Registration Portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (provincial DPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Circular No. 247/2016/TT-BTC: enterprise registration fee of VND 100,000 (approximately US$ 4) plus authorized administrative publication and dossier-processing charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, certified Vietnamese translation, and consular legalization of foreign-issued incorporation, UBO, and financial documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Vietnamese notary public, Department of Justice or notarization office, Embassy or Consulate of Viet Nam abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarization and translation according to provincial notary tariff schedules; foreign consular legalization pursuant to the Consular Fee Schedule under Circular No. 102/2017/TT-BTC and host-country service provider rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the Vietnamese charter (Điều lệ công ty), shareholding register, capital contribution schedule, and company seal notification attachment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bilingual charter drafting and statutory dossier compilation at standard market rate of US$ 500–700 per engagement plus notarization and certified copies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) filing and submission for the foreign-invested project, where transitionally required for colocation services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of Planning and Investment / Export Processing Zone or Industrial Zone Authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee applicable to investment registration under Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 02/2021/ND-CP; professional representation charges apply at prevailing market rates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (Articles 22, 25, 28, 45-47, 61-75, 77); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 (Articles 36-40); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Enterprise Registration (Articles 21-44); Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP on Investment Regulation (Articles 14-30); Circular No. 02/2022/TT-BKHDT on enterprise registration forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI); National Enterprise Registration Portal (NERP) at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; National Foreign Investment Information System (NFIIS) at nfiis.mpi.gov.vn.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Form I-1) with Company Charter (Dieu le cua cong ty) and List of Members (Form I-3); separate Application for Investment Registration Certificate (Form I-1/I-2) under the Investment Law for foreign-invested projects.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a standard limited liability company in the information technology service sector. Charter capital must be a positive amount approved by the members and must be fully contributed within 90 days after the Enterprise Registration Certificate is issued. There is no escrow account requirement; contribution is made by bank transfer to the company's designated corporate bank account and evidenced by a capital contribution statement. For data-center colocation projects, the registered capital must be consistent with the project scale and investment feasibility, and the DPI may reject the application if the capital is manifestly inadequate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 01/2025/NQ-HDTV OF THE MEMBERS' COUNCIL OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, adopted by unanimous written consent of all members holding 100% of charter capital on [date], at [address], Vietnam. Upon due deliberation, the Members' Council resolves that: (1) Charter Capital: the company shall adopt an initial charter capital of VND [amount], allocated among the members as set out in the Company Charter, and all members shall contribute the registered capital in full within 90 days from issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate by lawful bank transfers to the company's account. (2) Registered Office: the company's permanent registered office shall be [full Vietnam address], which is the location of the principal data-center facility and is lawfully leased/owned by the company. (3) Officers: [Name] is appointed as General Director and legal representative; [Name] is appointed as Chief Accountant; and [Name] is appointed as Compliance Officer, each to serve until removed by a subsequent resolution of the Members' Council. (4) Banking: the General Director is authorised to open corporate bank accounts in the name of the company and to execute banking mandates and payment instruments. (5) Seal: the company shall adopt an official seal, and the General Director shall file the seal specimen with the Department of Planning and Investment as required. (6) Registration Actions: the General Director shall prepare, sign, and pursue all investment registration, enterprise registration, tax registration, and ancillary approvals necessary for legal formation and operation. This Resolution becomes effective upon adoption and shall be included in the company's corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Registration Certificate application for foreign-invested limited liability company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via the National Foreign Investment Information System (NFIIS) or direct e-lodgement window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the investment dossier for a foreign-invested LLC. The package must include a formal application for the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), an investment project proposal, financial capacity documentation of the foreign investor, a draft investment site arrangement (lease or intended lease memorandum), and evidence of ability to implement the data-center project. The DPI will review market-access conditions under the negative-list approach and issue the IRC (or reject with written reasons). Submit using Form I-1 and I-2 under Decree 31/2021/ND-CP. Provide notarised English-to-Vietnamese translations of all foreign documents.
required_dossiers: Application for Investment Registration Certificate (Form I-1)
Investment Project Proposal (Form I-2)
Incorporation certificate or personal identification of each foreign investor
Latest audited financial statements or bank proof of financial ability of the investor
Draft site lease agreement, land-use right certificate, or letter of intent from the intended lessor
Detailed data-center project description including planned Tier rating, total rack capacity, and construction plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a query or request for amendment, correct the required documents and resubmit within the stated period (generally 30 days). If the IRC is denied, the investor may file a written appeal with the MPI within 30 days of receiving the refusal, or submit a revised project proposal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Company Charter and First Board Resolution of the Members' Council
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Members' Council of the company in a private corporate capacity; ratified before a notary where charter or law so requires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a valid meeting or obtain unanimous written consent from all founding members. Adopt the Company Charter in Vietnamese, the First Board Resolution defining charter capital, registered office, and officer appointments, and the List of Members. Ensure the charter contains the standard mandatory clauses under Article 25 of Law on Enterprises 2020, including company name, address, lines of business, charter capital, contributed capital of each member, legal representation, governance structure, and dispute resolution mechanism. Notarise the charter and member signatories if the parties so elect; notarisation of the charter is not a legal prerequisite for enterprise registration, but notarised forms are commonly required for subsequent bank and land filings.
required_dossiers: Company Charter (Dieu le cong ty) signed by all members or their authorised representatives
First Board Resolution / Written Consent of all Members
List of Members (Form I-3) identifying each member, nationality, capital contribution, and legal representative
Certificate of Investment Registration certificate obtained in Step 1
Valid identification documents of each member and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Charter defects identified at registration must be remedied by issuing a rectifying resolution and re-signing the charter before resubmission. If a notary identifies legal defects, the documents must be corrected and signed again; no government remedy is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of enterprise registration dossier to the Department of Planning and Investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via the National Enterprise Registration Portal (NERP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn, select 'New Enterprise Registration' for a limited liability company, and complete Application for Enterprise Registration (Form I-1). Upload the charter, list of members, IRC, lease/site documentation, and relevant resolutions. Digitally sign and submit. The DPI examines the dossier against the checklist in Article 21 of Decree 01/2021/ND-CP. If valid, the ERC is issued within three working days; if invalid, the applicant receives a formal notice listing all errors.
required_dossiers: Application for Enterprise Registration (Form I-1)
Company Charter
List of Members (Form I-3)
Investment Registration Certificate
Lease agreement or written permission from the building owner for the registered office address
Valid identity documents of the legal representative and members
Power of attorney if an appointed agent signs the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The DPI must reply in writing if the dossier is incomplete. The applicant must complete all corrections and resubmit within 30 days. If the applicant misses the deadline, a new dossier must be filed. A contested rejection may be appealed administratively to the MPI or challenged before an administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Enterprise Registration Certificate and publication on national enterprise informatisation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI); National Enterprise Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the DPI issues the ERC, collect the original certificate from the DPI office or download the duly issued electronic version. The system automatically publishes the company registration record on the National Enterprise Registration Portal; the applicant must verify such publication within 30 days. Confirm that the tax identification number is automatically inserted into the ERC upon issuance. Store the ERC in the statutory corporate records of the company.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate issued by DPI
No additional document required for publication; the DPI system performs publication
Copy of the IRC if cross-referenced in the publication record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is not performed automatically after 30 days, submit a written request to the DPI requiring it to carry out the publication, and, if necessary, file a complaint with the MPI. Errors appearing in the published data must be corrected through the DPI's re-publication procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Charter capital contribution and opening of bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management; commercial bank; DPI for capital contribution notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name and deposit the charter capital in full within 90 days of the ERC issuance date. Obtain a bank statement or investment capital contribution confirmation from the bank. The General Director must ensure that the amount actually contributed matches the charter and List of Members. After the deadline, if the capital is not fully paid, the members are proportionately required to use their entitlements accordingly; if capital is contributed late, the company must file a capital contribution notification with the DPI and correct the enterprise registration record.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Resolution opening the bank account and designating signatories
Bank account opening forms and customer due-diligence documents
Bank-issued capital contribution confirmation
Tax registration form (issued automatically via ERC tax number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the 90-day contribution deadline is missed, the non-contributing member loses voting and profit-sharing rights corresponding to the unpaid portion; the company must prepare a revised capital structure resolution and notify the DPI. If the bank rejects the account opening, rectify customer due-diligence documents and apply to another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company seal creation and seal specimen notification to the DPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI); company management
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the ERC is issued, manufacture the corporate seal at a licensed seal-engraving establishment. Complete the Seal Specimen Notification Form (Form I-5 under Decree 01/2021/ND-CP) and file it with the DPI within 15 days from the date of seal creation. The DPI records the seal specimen on the national enterprise information system. The seal must be used and kept according to Articles 44-45 of Law on Enterprises 2020.
required_dossiers: Seal Specimen Notification Form (Form I-5)
Enterprise Registration Certificate
Written confirmation of issuance/difficulties from the engraving establishment if notification is delayed
Valid identity of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI requests additional information, provide a notarised explanation. In case of late notification of the seal specimen, the company may be exposed to administrative fines; the notification should be filed as soon as discovered and, where necessary, the DPI may require a formal declaration of the late filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical facility and civil-defence licensing: construction permit, fire-safety certificate and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Construction; Fire Police Department (C07) under the Ministry of Public Security; provincial People's Committee for building occupation/clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a data-center building or renovated hosting facility, obtain a construction permit from the provincial Department of Construction before any conversion or construction. After physical completion, engage the Fire Police Department for a technical safety inspection and obtain a Fire Safety Certificate to operate the facility. For indoor workplace clearance, comply with local civil-defence requirements, including structural load checks, emergency exit plans, and backup generator safety approval. These physical licenses are distinct from the enterprise registration and are mandatory before the data-center becomes operational.
required_dossiers: Construction permit application with architectural and engineering plans
Structural plans and load-bearing calculations for server hall floors
Fire-safety design dossier approved by the Fire Police Department
Certificate of completed construction or as-built drawings
Application for fire-safety inspection and pre-operational inspection
Workplace / occupational health and safety assessment by an authorised agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire-safety inspection identifies deficiencies, undertake corrective works and request re-inspection. If the construction permit is refused, modify the plans and resubmit. A denial of the fire-safety certificate may be administratively appealed to the provincial Fire Police Department or the Ministry of Public Security within the prescribed time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental registration and discharge compliance certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) / People's Committee of the province; environmental police under the Ministry of Public Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the environmental classification of the data-center project. For a Tier-3/4 colocation facility with backup diesel generators and cooling towers, the project typically falls under the 'environmental registration' category rather than a full EIA. Prepare an Environmental Registration Report with details on water discharge from cooling systems, emissions from backup generators, battery and e-waste handling, and solid waste management. Submit the registration to the provincial DONRE or the delegated district-level state agency. Obtain the environmental registration acknowledgment before commissioning the center. If the capacity or power load exceeds thresholds that push the project into the full EIA list, a full Environmental Impact Assessment must be carried out under the Law on Environmental Protection 2020.
required_dossiers: Environmental Registration Report (Bao cao dang ky moi truong)
Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate
Project site layout and equipment list
Wastewater discharge and water management plan
Diesel generator specifications and backup power emission calculations
Hazardous waste / battery disposal contract with a licensed environmental service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DONRE classifies the project as requiring a full EIA, commission an EIA consultant, submit a comprehensive EIA report, and obtain the approval decision before operation. If the environmental registration is rejected or queried, supplement the technical information and resubmit; unresolved denials may be contested by administrative appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Information and Communications (MIC) is the sector policy authority, but a pure data-center colocation service under ISIC 6209 does not require a telecommunications or Internet service licence. The operative industrial authorisations are issued by: Department of Construction (construction permit), Fire Police Department C07 (fire-safety certificate), and Provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (environmental registration).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate 'data-center operating license' is required for pure colocation and bare-metal hosting activities under current Vietnamese law; the Enterprise Registration Certificate together with the Fire-Safety Certificate and Environmental Registration constitute the statutory operating authorisation. If the company later offers value-added telecommunications or internet content services, a telecommunications service licence under Decree 72/2013/ND-CP as amended would become mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Environmental Registration (Dang ky moi truong) for low/medium-impact projects; a full EIA is required only if installed electrical capacity, area of real estate, or wastewater volumes exceed the thresholds in Decree 08/2022/ND-CP. Most Tier-3/4 data centers fall within Registration, subject to a project-specific threshold review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Standards apply under QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT for domestic wastewater, QCVN 01:2021/BCT for industrial wastewater, QCVN 06:2021/BCT for volatile organic compounds and exhaust gases, and QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT for air emissions from diesel generators. Hazardous waste (spent batteries, e-waste, transformer oil) must be declared and handled by licensed waste-treatment enterprises under Decree 08/2022/ND-CP and the Law on Environmental Protection 2020. Cooling-water discharge to municipal sewers must meet local sewer-use permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory prerequisites: (i) Fire-Safety Certificate issued by the Fire Police Department (C07) after an on-site inspection; (ii) construction permit and completion inspection for new/renovated buildings; (iii) structural load certification for server floors and raised floors; (iv) workplace occupational-health and safety clearance covering electric safety, back-up generator ventilation, confined-space protocols, and emergency evacuation drills; and (v) electrical engineering inspection and commissioning certificate by a licensed electrical authority. No additional civil-defence clearance is triggered by the data-center activity itself.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT; Tổng cục Thuế) under the Ministry of Finance; primary e-services portal: National Electronic Tax Portal (eTax) at https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; e-invoice portal: https://hoadon.gdt.gov.vn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested LLC: (1) obtain Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) or the Industrial/Export Processing Zone Authority; (2) obtain Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) from DPI; (3) the Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế – MST) is automatically generated and unified with the enterprise code upon ERC issuance; (4) complete electronic tax registration (Form 05/ĐK-THT) on the eTax portal, declaring VAT, CIT declaration method, and fiscal year; (5) procure a certified digital signature (USB token) for e-declarations and e-invoicing; (6) register the e-invoice template and e-invoice service provider with GDT before issuing invoices. Foreign contractors without a Vietnamese legal entity must separately register Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) with the local tax office using Form 01/ĐK-NTL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam does not operate U.S.-style check-the-box elections or hybrid-mismatch elections; LLCs are mandatorily taxed at entity level (CIT at 20%). Available statutory elections include: (i) VAT calculation method election – credit (input-deduction) method is compulsory for enterprises with annual revenue above VND 1 billion; direct (output-minus-input or add-on) method is available for qualified small taxpayers with revenue below VND 1 billion; (ii) Foreign Contractor Tax method election (deemed/knock-off method vs. normal accounting method) for eligible foreign contractors; (iii) election of CIT incentive regimes and preferential rates (high-tech zone, export processing zone, supporting industry certificates) subject to meeting statutory conditions; (iv) election to keep books and declare tax in a foreign currency with GDT approval. Elections are made by submission of prescribed forms via the eTax portal and, once adopted, generally apply for the whole tax period unless amended with GDT consent.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT – thuế GTGT) under the Law on VAT No. 13/2008/QH12, as amended; data-center colocation leasing and server hosting are standard-rated IT/business services subject to 10% VAT and are excluded from the temporary 8% reduced-rate relief (Decree 15/2022 and extension decrees, as IT and telecommunications services are carved out).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for a corporate LLC: VAT registration is compulsory before commencing business, immediately upon ERC issuance; VND 100,000,000/year turnover threshold applies only to households, individual entrepreneurs, and small non-corporate business households under the direct VAT method. Foreign-invested LLCs must register for VAT regardless of projected revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC, effective 1 July 2022. All e-invoices must be generated in standardized XML format containing a mandatory QR code and must be registered on GDT's national e-invoice portal or with a GDT-certified e-invoice service provider. Coded e-invoices require API-transmitted XML data to the GDT portal at issuance to receive the tax-authority code before forwarding to customers; retail and cash-register invoices are subject to real-time (near-immediate) transmission to GDT. Uncoded e-invoices must be transmitted to GDT within the declaratory period (monthly or quarterly). Corporate digital signatures (HiSign) are compulsory; the real-time cash-register invoice clearance architecture applies to on-premises retail payments, not to pure B2B colocation billing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to (a) exported goods physically shipped abroad; (b) services exported or supplied to foreign organizations or individuals and consumed entirely outside Vietnam, including international transport; and (c) services directly connected to exported goods. To claim 0%, taxpayers must evidence the export with: a signed export sales contract; for goods, a full customs file (electronic customs declaration, customs-sealed commercial invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, certificate of origin where required); for services, a written contract with the foreign party, proof that the services are performed and consumed outside Vietnam with benefits accruing outside Vietnam, and non-cash cross-border payment evidence. Important limitation: data-center colocation and rack-space leasing deliverables are physically supplied and consumed inside Vietnam (server racks located in Vietnam); such services have place of supply in Vietnam and are taxed at 10% VAT even if billed to a foreign customer. 0% treatment is not available merely because the customer is offshore; only genuine offshore services (e.g., remote technical services consumed abroad and not benefiting any Vietnamese party) may qualify, and the burden of proof lies with the taxpayer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic customs export declaration with customs clearance confirmation)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or equivalent international transport document (evidencing physical export)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Swift MT103 / FX repatriation proof (foreign-currency remittance received)
Export Sales Contract (signed with foreign buyer, stating Incoterms and payment terms)
Service Performance / Consumption Certificate (for offshore services, attesting consumption outside Vietnam with no Vietnamese beneficiary)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: GDT applies risk-based pre-refund audits and tax inspections to export zero-rating claims; missing bills of lading, customs declarations, or FX remittance files trigger automatic disallowance. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims constitute tax evasion under the Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 125/2020/ND-CP: administrative penalty of 20% of the evaded or unduly refunded VAT, plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day calculated retrospectively from the refund or offset date; the refund is clawed back in full with interest; the taxpayer may be barred from VAT refund treatment for up to 12 months. Customs false-export penalties under Decree 128/2020/ND-CP apply in addition, including fines up to VND 200 million per violation and confiscation in serious cases. Criminal tax evasion under Penal Code 2015 (Article 200) exposes individuals (CEO, CFO, chief accountant) to fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to 7 years; legal entities may be fined up to VND 15 billion and/or suspended from operations for up to 3 years. The statute of limitations is 5 years for tax declaration inspection and 10 years for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam), Department of Foreign Exchange Management (Vụ Quản lý Ngoại hối), 49 Ly Thai To Street, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam. SBV exercises exclusive statutory authority over foreign exchange administration, authorizes commercial banks to act as authorized dealers in foreign currency, and regulates all foreign borrowing, capital account transactions, cross-border payments, and profit remittances under the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 04/2003/PL-UBTVQH11 as amended by Ordinance No. 06/2013/UBTVQH13, together with Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN and Circular 12/2022/TT-NHNN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vietnam maintains de facto current-account convertibility while retaining strict capital-account controls. For a foreign-invested LLC engaged in data center colocation leasing to offshore tenants, USD-denominated service export revenue is freely receivable into a locally held foreign currency account but must be repatriated to Vietnam within the statutory window; conversion of VND to foreign currency for profit remittance is permitted only after annual external audit completion, corporate income tax finalization, and a declaration that all taxes, social insurance premiums, and labor obligations have been settled. Dividend and profit remittances are effected in the original foreign currency through the entity's Direct Foreign Investment Capital Account. Offshore convertibility of the Vietnamese dong remains absent: VND is non-deliverable outside Vietnam, offshore NDF markets referencing VND are not legally recognized by SBV, and the onshore interbank FX market is managed within a daily trading band (currently plus/minus 5% around the SBV reference rate). Capital account items, including charter capital increases, foreign shareholder loans, equity transfers, and liquidation proceeds, all require prior SBV registration or licensing; early or unreported equity repatriation is treated as a foreign exchange breach subject to administrative fines and potential criminal exposure under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP and Penal Code provisions on currency smuggling.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN (implementing Ordinance on Foreign Exchange), export proceeds, including cross-border service export receipts from data center colocation and bare-metal server hosting supplied to non-resident customers, must be credited to a licensed foreign currency account located in Vietnam within 90 days from the date the export service is performed/perfection or the invoice becomes due. The statutory rule does not impose an automatic conversion ratio for private service exporters: the full 100% of export proceeds must be repatriated to the local foreign currency account, after which the enterprise may retain USD to fund permissible foreign currency obligations (payments for imported bandwidth, power infrastructure, equipment, and overseas vendor invoices) or may sell USD to the authorized bank for VND. Mandatory conversion to VND applies narrowly, e.g., to certain petroleum exports and state-owned trading houses, and does not apply to a private data center operator. The enterprise must submit a quarterly export-proceeds status report to the PBX branch where the account is held if requested; non-repatriation beyond 90 days triggers administraive penalties up to VND 200,000,000 and potential revocation of the foreign currency account license, and the underreported or unrepatriated amount may be treated as a foreign exchange violation requiring remedial sale of the receivable at the central bank rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / FDI Capital Account (Tài khoản vốn đầu tư trực tiếp), USD Operational Account, VND Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account / Operational Account (USD & VND), Foreign Loan Disbursement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account / Operational Account (USD & VND), Trade Finance Account under L/C facilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Techcombank (Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank)
Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (VND & USD), e-Banking Settlement Account
Operational Account (USD & VND), secondary clearing account for local vendor payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW feasibility rating for offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currenxie, Intergiro) as primary treasury or clearing rails. Vietnamese foreign exchange law and Decree 70/2014/ND-CP restrict resident enterprises from holding or using offshore payment accounts for transactions that should be settled through SBV-supervised channels; Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN mandates that cross-border service export proceeds be credited to an authorized bank in Vietnam, making an offshore EMI account the legal equivalent of unrepatriated export proceeds if funds remain offshore beyond 90 days. Offshore EMIs are neither licensed nor regulated by SBV for dong clearing, cannot open VND nostro accounts without a local partner, and generally cannot originate compliant MT103 payments bearing Vietnamese purpose codes. A narrow permissible use exists: low-value recurring international invoices (e.g., domain renewal, software subscriptions) may be paid via a licensed international payment intermediary only if the intermediary holds a Vietnamese e-wallet/payment intermediary license under Decree 101/2012/ND-CP and Circular 39/2014/TT-NHNN. The sanctioned architecture is full onshore banking with SBV-licensed authorized banks, supplemented, at most, by a licensed foreign payment intermediary for micro-payments; treasury concentration offshore or use of an unlicensed EMI is classified as a foreign exchange offense.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the statutory legal representative is mandatory for initial account opening of a foreign-invested LLC across all Vietnamese commercial banks. Under Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15, Decree 10/2023/ND-CP, and AML guiding Circular 11/2022/TT-NHNN, the legal representative (or a clearly authorized director holding a notarized Power of Attorney) must appear at the bank branch in person, present original passports, the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC), the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), the company seal specimen registration, and execute wet-ink signature cards and AML interviews before an authorized bank officer. No fully remote opening exists for foreign-owned companies; video-KYC is accepted only as a supplemental documentary step and cannot replace the physical interview. Any subsequent addition of a non-resident signatory or any change in ultimate beneficial ownership (≥25% natural persons) triggers a renewed physical verification, supported by notarized translations. For day-to-day operations after onboarding, e-banking with OTP/certificate authentication and pre-registered IP whitelisting is permitted; physical attendance is not required for routine transactions, but the bank retains the right to summon the legal representative for suspicion-driven interviews with 48 hours notice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is a corporate entity in a high-risk or tax-haven jurisdiction (BVI, Cayman, Seychelles) or an opaque multi-tier holding chain without clear attribution of natural persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SBV-prescribed Ultimate Beneficial Owner declaration identifying all natural persons holding 25% or more of the chain; notarized Vietnamese translations of foreign corporate registry extracts (Certificate of Good Standing); full organizational chart from the ultimate individual down to the Vietnamese LLC; source of wealth dossier comprising audited financial statements of the shareholder and bank reference letters from the shareholder's home financial institution; notarized passports of UBOs; statement of no adverse media and PEP check results from a reputable screening database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business scope (data center colocation/leasing) and expected transaction profile dominated by frequent cross-border USD credits from unrelated foreign tenants
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master colocation agreements and per-rack service contracts with foreign enterprise customers; tenant KYC file including customer registry extract and passport copies of tenant signatories; invoice schedule with monthly recurring charge pattern; proof of physical operations comprising the data center lease agreement, power purchase agreement (PPA), and utilities billing; SBV-compliant FX transaction declaration forms; bank documentary evidence of the underlying service performance (billing records, SLA reports).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large charter capital injection or shareholder loan disbursement occurring within weeks of incorporation without proportionate evidence of funding capacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital call and the exact timing; executed capital contribution agreement filed with the Department of Planning and Investment; SBV Foreign Loan Registration Certificate for any shareholder loan issued under Circular 12/2022/TT-NHNN; SWIFT MT103 credit messages matched to the FDI capital account; certified source of funds comprising shareholder audited financial statements, dividend distribution minutes, or asset disposition deeds; tax identification certificate of the Vietnamese LLC; statement from the authorized bank confirming the FDI account number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage outbound trade payments (prepayment to overseas equipment suppliers for servers, UPS, cooling, and racks) submitted before import documentation exists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-Forma Invoice and purchase order from each supplier; executed import contract referencing Incoterms 2020; board resolution authorizing the trade prepayment; bank's LC or T/T application signed and stamped by the authorized legal representative; prior customs declaration history (or declaration number if goods already in transit); Equivalence import/export code assigned by customs; supplier due-diligence file including supplier registry and contact verification; sworn attestation that goods are for operational use in the licensed data center facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a Power of Attorney signatory rather than the registered legal representative, particularly for high-value FX transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Power of Attorney executed in compliance with Vietnamese Civil Code 2015 and Notarization Law, expressly listing the transactional scope (opening accounts, signing FX contracts, issuing L/Cs); legalized translation into Vietnamese if executed abroad; passport and residency documents of both the grantor (statutory legal representative) and the attorney-in-fact; specimen signature card registered at the bank with identity verification; corporation seal used on the PoA matched with the seal registration certificate at the Department of Planning and Investment; board resolution ratifying the delegation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high volume of round-tripped funds or frequent recourse to third-party payments (asking the bank to credit amounts to unrelated beneficiaries) inconsistent with a colocation fee stream
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal-purpose letter (Cam kết mục đích sử dụng vốn) stating the commercial rationale for each third-party payment; end-to-end invoice trail from tenant invoice to the eventual supplier/bank settlement; service verification certificates from data center management systems; an explanatory memorandum from the CFO identifying the treasury topology; updated UBO declarations confirming no informal shareholders; commitment to implement quarterly transaction-profile reporting to the bank's compliance unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity and shareholder-loan funding must be routed through the Direct Foreign Investment Capital Account maintained at the primary authorized dealer bank (FDI Capital Account). The LLC must open this account after issuance of the IRC/ERC and register every capital call with the bank before receipt. For charter capital: credit via SWIFT MT103 with the purpose code 'Investment Capital Contribution – FDI Account' and documentary support comprising the certificate of investment, enterprise registration certificate, board resolution on capital call, and a receipt-purpose letter. For intercompany shareholder loans: obtain an SBV Foreign Loan Registration Certificate (Form D-1, issued under Circular 12/2022/TT-NHNN) before disbursement; loan proceeds must be received into the registered borrowing account or the FDI account and may not be credited to any private offshore account. VND-equivalent and USD-equivalent reporting thresholds apply: all transactions equal or exceeding USD 10,000 must be individually justified with a transaction purpose certificate (Giấy đề nghị xác nhận mục đích chuyển tiền) and the bank will file the report to SBV's Foreign Exchange Information System. Non-compliance before receipt (e.g., upfront utilization of funds from an unregistered loan) invalidates the future tax deductibility of interest and triggers fines under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP. For robust capital deployment, structure the initial capital contribution in two to three tranches matching build-out milestones; each tranche must be fully evidenced with board minutes and a revised capital utilization schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for imported servers, networking equipment, environmental control systems, software licenses, and cloud interconnect fees use the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for direct telegraphic transfers (T/T) to overseas suppliers under 30-90 day terms; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or deferred payment, UCP600-compliant) issued by the Vietnamese bank in favor of the supplier, particularly for high-value hardware import batches; (iii) standby L/Cs or bank guarantees for equipment lease and data center infrastructure financing; (iv) direct debits and domestic NAPAS clearing for local vendor and utility payments in VND. Before any FX outward payment, the bank requires underlying trade documents: an import contract or agreement, supplier invoice or packing list, customs declaration (or proof of service receipt for intangible expenses), and a board resolution for payments exceeding VND 500 million. Recurring cross-border O&M expenses (bandwidth, interconnect, vendor-remote-hand) may be aggregated in a quarterly settlement statement with a schedule of services rendered. USD vendor payments are paid from the USD operational account; VND limitations are avoided for foreign beneficiaries except for a narrowly defined list of local-currency remittance cases permitted under Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN. Settlement to countries under OFAC/UN sanctions is automatically blocked by correspondent bank filters; screen all counterparties and include standard denial-of-service sanctions language in supplier terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/VND outright forward contracts with licensed commercial banks, tenor up to 180 days, governed by Circular 02/2018/TT-NHNN; physically settled only, requiring an underlying trade or investment transaction for hedging eligibility.
Onshore FX swaps (spot vs. forward USD/VND) with an authorized credit institution for treasury liquidity management and matching of receivable/liability maturities.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/VND) combined with an underlying foreign currency loan, subject to SBV approval and only with a licensed counterparty executing the derivative as part of a documented borrowing facility.
Foreign currency interest-rate swaps or options permissible only when ancillary to a registered cross-border loan and executed inside Vietnam with SBV-authorized dealing room supervision.

NO offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Vietnamese dong are permissible or enforceable in Vietnam. VND is non-convertible offshore; attempting to place NDF positions through an offshore parent is illegal and exposes the Vietnamese entity to FX sanction - all hedging must be executed onshore for physical USD/VND settlement.
Internal natural hedging: manage net USD positions tightly by denominating receivables and payable in USD with matched monthly settlement to reduce derivative counterparty reliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Business Operation Report (Báo cáo tình hình doanh nghiệp) with updated ownership, charter capital, and UBO-linked information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Business Registration Portal / provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) where the foreign-invested LLC is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January – 31 March each calendar year, relating to the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 5,000,000–10,000,000 (approx. USD 210–420) under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; persistent non-submission can result in suspension or administrative revocation of registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Fee declaration and payment (Lệ phí môn bài) based on charter capital tier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direct Taxation Department of the General Department of Taxation (provincial tax authority where the LLC's head office is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 January each year; newly established LLCs are exempt for the first year and must submit an exemption declaration within 30 days of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount plus administrative fines for late filing under the Law on Tax Administration 38/2019/QH14; repeated non-compliance may trigger tax debt enforcement measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (Báo cáo tài chính đã kiểm toán)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Authority, Statistics Office, and Department of Planning and Investment where applicable; a copy is also retained by the independent audit firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 90 days after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year entities must submit by 31 March. Audited statements must accompany the annual corporate income tax finalization return due on 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission incurs administrative fines under the Law on Accounting and tax administration regulations (typically VND 5,000,000–10,000,000). Failure to file audited financial statements also invalidates eligibility for certain government incentives and may result in tax finalization penalty assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested enterprises in Vietnam, regardless of revenue or asset size, are required by Decree 17/2012/ND-CP to have their annual financial statements audited by an independent audit firm. The foreign-invested LLC’s FDI status alone triggers the mandatory audit; no additional revenue or asset threshold applies beyond that requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS), Law on Accounting 88/2015/QH13, and Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC. IFRS is not a mandatory statutory framework for a private foreign-invested LLC; it may only be used for consolidated group reporting or where specifically permitted by regulatory decisions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for a standard Vietnamese LLC. Under the Enterprise Law 2020 and Decree 01/2021/ND-CP, any transfer of membership interest or change in beneficial ownership, charter-capital ratio, or ultimate controller must be registered with the provincial DPI within 10 days of the change. The Annual Enterprise Business Operation Report filed by 31 March serves as the annual ownership confirmation, restating member identities and UBO data for the prior fiscal year. Beneficial ownership details must also be maintained in the company’s AML customer due diligence records pursuant to the Anti-Money Laundering Law 2013 and implementing guidelines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members showing legal name, address, national ID or incorporation number, contribution ratio, and date of admission
Register of Directors / Legal Representatives containing appointment, revocation, and contact details of all current and former authorized signatories
Minute Book recording meetings and resolutions of the Members' Council and any members' decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–800 per year for registered-office address service and corporate secretarial support within Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City; actual market fee depends on provider scope and transaction volume.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–5,000 per year for a medium-sized foreign-invested LLC engaged in data-center colocation leasing, including statutory year-end audit, management letter, and tax finalization support.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax rate is 20%. Qualifying data center and information technology activities may access preferential rates of 10% for up to 15 years, with a 4-year full tax exemption and 9-year 50% reduction, if the enterprise is located in an information technology park, high-tech zone, or satisfies the Law on High Technology and Decree 218/2013/ND-CP incentive conditions. Small and micro enterprises may also benefit from reduced rates in windows provided by domestic legislation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Provisional Declaration – Form No. 01/TNDN; filed electronically via the General Department of Taxation eTax portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 30th day following the end of each quarter (30 April, 30 July, 30 October, 30 January for a calendar-year taxpayer).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number, registered name, address, and data-center establishment information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the foreign-invested LLC's Vietnamese tax identification number and confirm no liquidation proceedings are pending.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accrued gross revenue from colocation rack leasing, bare-metal hosting, power/cooling pass-through charges, and managed infrastructure fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue in accordance with Vietnamese Accounting Standards; exclude VAT and adjust cross-border prepaid related-party receivables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible expenses including data-center electricity, cooling, maintenance, staff costs, insurance, depreciation of servers and racks, and third-party bandwidth.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only substantiated, legitimate invoices are deductible; related-party charges must comply with Decree 132/2020/ND-CP transfer pricing levels.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated profit for the quarter after applying revenue less deductible costs and any loss carryforward or incentive adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 80% annual minimum provisional payment rule; state the effective preferential CIT rate if a 10% rate has been formally approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT calculated by multiplying provisional taxable income by the applicable corporate income tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty relief applies to deductible royalties or interest, record reduced withholding options but do not offset foreign tax credits at the provisional stage unless specifically authorized.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing of the quarterly provisional declaration triggers administrative fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP up to VND 20,000,000 plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on any underscheduled amount. Persistent non-payment may lead to coercive bank blocking and travel bans.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return – Form No. 02/TNDN; filed electronically via the General Department of Taxation eTax portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 90th day after the end of the fiscal year (usually 31 March for a calendar-year taxpayer if the fiscal year ends on 31 December).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total annual revenue from data center colocation, hosting, and ancillary technical services; reconciling to audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report global revenue derived in Vietnam only; intercompany service revenue to offshore affiliates must be fully disclosed on separate schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line B – Deductible Costs and Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full-year deductible expenditures: facility depreciation, lease of land or building, employee salaries, utilities, network interconnect fees, and regulated insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible expenses (e.g., dividends, certain provisions, fines) must be added back. Directors should certify the economic substance of every cost line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual taxable profit computed as gross revenue less deductible expenses, plus non-deductible adjustments, less tax-exempt income and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards cannot exceed five years; any unused balance expires. Profits attributable to colocation services cannot be shifted to low-tax subsidiary jurisdictions without documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Standard 20% or preferential 10% rate if the data center qualifies for the technology/software incentive regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim preferential tax rates strictly on the portion of income derived from qualifying activities; split method must be approved by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line E – Quarterly Prepayments and Final CIT Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of quarterly provisional CIT payments and final balance due or receivable after reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If quarterly prepayments were below 80% of the final liability, an additional late-payment interest charge of 0.03% per day applies to the shortfall.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line F – Foreign Tax Credits / DTA Reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits allowed for foreign taxes paid on income earned overseas (if any) and treaty reductions applied on dividends, royalties, and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the necessary documents (Certificate of Residency, tax authority approvals) with the annual return to claim reduced withholding or credit; otherwise the return may be subject to re-assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late finalization fines range from VND 4,000,000 to VND 20,000,000; under-declared tax may be subject to an additional administrative penalty of up to 25% of the omitted tax plus late-payment interest at 0.03%/day. Criminal tax evasion provisions may apply for deliberate misstatement exceeding VND 100,000,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% domestic final withholding tax applied to dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders; non-resident individuals are subject to 5% personal income tax on dividend distributions. Most Vietnamese tax treaties reduce the domestic corporate dividend withholding tax to 5% where the beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the share capital, and 10% in all other qualifying cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA) reduction, the foreign recipient shareholder must produce an authenticated Certificate of Residency (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the receiving jurisdiction. The Vietnamese LLC (payer) submits the TRC and a formal DTA relief application to the local General Department of Taxation office before making the dividend distribution. Once approved, the payer withholds at the treaty-reduced rate; if already withheld at the statutory rate, the foreign shareholder may file a consequential refund under the Vietnamese Tax Administration Law within three years of payment. Supporting documentation should include the LLC's board resolution, audited financial statements for distributable profits, and evidence of the investor's beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding rules under Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC impose a 5% Foreign Contractor Tax CIT on interest payments to non-resident lenders and a 10% CIT plus 5% VAT on royalties paid to non-resident IP owners. Many Vietnamese tax treaties cap interest withholding at 10% and royalties at 5% to 10%, depending on the asset or effective reciprocity conditions. Data center payments characterized as 'right to use industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment' may be treated as royalties and thus attract the relevant domestic/treaty withholding rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File threshold: total revenue of at least VND 50 billion in a fiscal year OR total related-party transaction value of at least VND 30 billion. Mandatory Master File threshold: ultimate parent's consolidated global revenue of at least VND 18,000 billion. Below these thresholds, taxpayers must still file an annual related-party transaction declaration and maintain a sufficiently documented pricing policy.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) framework similar to the UAE or BVI, but its General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the transfer pricing rules in Decree 132/2020/ND-CP require commercial arrangements to reflect actual economic substance. For a data center colocation LLC, the entity must demonstrate real decision-making, qualified personnel, physical control over the facility, assumption of operating and market risk, and the capacity to generate profits independent of offshore affiliate instructions. The tax authority may recharacterize routing structures, deny treaty benefits, and disregard the LLC as a façade if substance is absent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting cash colocation fees or server hosting revenue from CIT returns, inflating deductibles through fake supplier invoices, creating undisclosed offshore bank accounts, or submitting a fraudulent annual tax finalization with declared revenue below the actual billing records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The taxpayer is liable for back-taxes for up to 10 years, an administrative penalty of up to 25% of under-declared tax, late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and criminal penalties under Article 200 of the Penal Code: fines from VND 100 million to VND 4.5 billion, imprisonment from 6 months to 20 years for tax evasion exceeding VND 100 million, and confiscation of instrumentalities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general managers, and chief accountants who authorize fraudulent filings face personal criminal prosecution, civil restitution of unpaid taxes and penalties, travel bans, exit suspension, and seizure of personal assets when the corporate veil is pierced as a vehicle for criminal tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling rack space and bare-metal servers to an offshore related operator at systematically depressed prices; charging excessive group management fees or intra-group royalties without transfer pricing documentation; failure to prepare Local File or Master File despite breaching the statutory thresholds; or arbitrarily selecting a pricing method that produces operating losses for five consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Department of Taxation may adjust taxable income to the arm's length level, impose additional CIT, apply late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and levy administrative fines for absent documentation under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP. Willful gross mispricing can escalate to criminal tax prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be individually called into tax audits, personally liable for tax shortfalls if they directed the intercompany pricing, subjected to prohibition from leaving Vietnam until outstanding amounts are settled, and criminally liable under tax evasion or fraud indictments where the filing was deliberately falsified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the VN LLC solely as a profit channel to remit distributions to a low-tax jurisdiction without operating any servers, personnel, procurement, or credit risk; routing colocation fees through the LLC without physical corporate substance or board decision-making in Vietnam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may apply the GAAR and substance-over-form doctrine to deny CIT incentives, disallow dividend treaty relief, reclassify revenue as taxable Vietnamese-sourced income, and impose penalties up to 25% of the underpaid tax together with late-payment interest. In egregious cases, business registration and data-center operating approvals may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors can be held personally responsible for all unpaid taxation and penalties when the LLC is treated as a sham; civil restitution, asset freezing, travel bans, and criminal fraud convictions may follow. Regulators may pierce the corporate veil to recover unlawful distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Foreign Currency and Professional Sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting untraceable cash payments for colocation services, knowingly hosting sanctioned counterparties without checking global watchlists, moving client funds through unlicensed money service businesses, or repatriating dividends without complying with the State Bank of Vietnam foreign exchange regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering and Decree 116/2013/ND-CP/amended decrees include monetary fines up to VND 3 billion, revocation of payment operation agreements, confiscation of illicit proceeds, and criminal penalties under relevant penal provisions. Non-resident remittances outside approved bank channels are also subject to exchange-control fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The data center's board and chief compliance officer face direct AML liability, personal fines, travel bans, disqualification from company management, and imprisonment where omissions facilitated money laundering or terrorist financing through the colocation infrastructure.
